about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Mustard Seed Honey Vinaigrette
recipes.summary: A glossy, sweet-sharp salad dressing of wholegrain mustard, honey and cider vinegar that keeps for a week.
steps: Whisk the mustard, honey, vinegar, salt and pepper in a bowl until smooth.
Pour the oil in a thin stream, whisking until the dressing is thick and glossy.
Stir in the shallot and taste, adding more honey or vinegar until balanced.
notes: Shake in a jar to emulsify again before using.
Keeps for 7 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Miso Sesame Dressing
recipes.summary: A creamy, savoury-sweet dressing of white miso, toasted sesame and rice vinegar for cabbage, greens and noodles.
steps: Whisk the miso, tahini, rice vinegar, soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil and ginger in a bowl.
Add the water a spoon at a time, whisking until the dressing is smooth and pourable.
Stir in the sesame seeds and taste.
notes: Thin with more water for noodles or leave thicker as a dip.
Keeps for 5 days in a jar in the fridge.

recipes.title: Green Goddess Dressing
recipes.summary: A thick herb dressing of yoghurt, avocado, parsley, chives and lemon that turns any salad into a feast.
steps: Blend the avocado, yoghurt, mayonnaise, herbs, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar and salt until smooth.
Add the water and blend again until the dressing is creamy and pourable.
Taste and add more lemon or salt.
notes: Pour over cos lettuce, boiled eggs or roast vegetables.
Keeps for 2 days in a jar in the fridge.

recipes.title: Japanese Style Ginger Carrot Dressing
recipes.summary: The orange, zingy dressing from the sushi bar, blended from carrot, fresh ginger and rice vinegar.
steps: Blend the carrots, onion, vinegar, soy sauce, ginger, honey, oils and water until smooth.
Taste, adding more vinegar or honey until bright and balanced.
Pour into a jar and chill.
notes: Spoon over iceberg lettuce or cabbage.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Ranch Dressing
recipes.summary: A cool and creamy herb dressing for crunchy salads, wings and raw vegetable platters.
steps: Whisk the buttermilk, sour cream and mayonnaise in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the garlic, herbs, onion powder, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Taste, then chill for 30 minutes so the flavour deepens.
notes: Thin with a little more buttermilk for a pourable dressing.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Thai Sweet Chilli Lime Dressing
recipes.summary: A sticky, tangy dressing of sweet chilli, lime and fish sauce for noodle salads and grilled meats.
steps: Warm the lime juice, sugar and fish sauce in a small pan for 2 minutes, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sweet chilli sauce, vinegar, garlic and chilli.
Cool, then whisk in the oil.
notes: Toss through cucumber and herb salads or noodles.
Keeps for 7 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Sweet Lime Fish Sauce Dressing
recipes.summary: The balanced sweet, sour, salty and spicy sauce for spring rolls, vermicelli bowls and grilled pork.

items: 2 red bird's eye chillies, finely chopped

steps: Stir the sugar into the warm water until it dissolves.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice and stir.
Taste and adjust, adding more lime for sour or sugar for sweet, then add the garlic, chilli and carrot.
Leave to infuse for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Taste it on a piece of cucumber to check the balance.
Keeps for 5 days in a jar in the fridge.

recipes.title: Greek Lemon and Oregano Vinaigrette
recipes.summary: The dressing for a horiatiki salad and grilled fish, with lemon, dried oregano and plenty of extra virgin olive oil.
steps: Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Whisk in the oil in a thin stream until thick and emulsified.
Taste and adjust the lemon.
notes: Also good over roast potatoes and grilled chicken.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Italian Balsamic Shallot Vinaigrette
recipes.summary: A rounded, slightly sweet vinaigrette of aged balsamic, sharp shallot and Dijon for bitter leaves.
steps: Combine the shallot, vinegar, mustard, honey, salt and pepper in a bowl and stir.
Slowly whisk in the oil until thick and glossy.
Taste, then use straight away or store.
notes: Leave the shallot in the vinegar for 5 minutes first to soften its bite.
Keeps for 7 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Mexican Quick Pickled Red Onions
recipes.summary: Pink, tangy onion rings in a lime and vinegar brine that lift tacos, eggs and rice bowls in half an hour.
steps: Pack the onions into a clean jar.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, oregano and garlic for 2 minutes, until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Pour the hot brine over the onions with the lime juice and press down until submerged.
Cool for 30 minutes, then chill.
notes: Ready to eat in 30 minutes, best after a day.
Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.

recipes.title: Japanese Asazuke Quick Pickled Cucumber
recipes.summary: Lightly salted cucumber with ginger and kombu-free seasoning, crisp and fresh in under an hour.
steps: Rub the cucumber slices with the salt in a bowl and leave for 15 minutes, until they release water.
Squeeze out the liquid with your hands.
Toss with the vinegar, soy sauce, ginger and chilli.
Chill for 20 minutes and sprinkle with sesame seeds to serve.
notes: Serve with steamed rice and miso soup.
Eat within 2 days for the best crunch.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Pickled Daikon and Carrot Sticks for Banh Mi
recipes.summary: Sweet, sour and crunchy matchsticks for banh mi, noodle bowls and rice plates.
steps: Toss the carrot and daikon with the salt and 1 tbsp sugar, and leave for 10 minutes, until slightly softened.
Rinse the vegetables well and squeeze them dry.
Stir the remaining sugar into the warm water and vinegar until dissolved.
Pack the vegetables into a jar and pour over the brine until covered.
Chill for 1 hour before using.
notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
The jar smells strong at first, but the smell fades.

recipes.title: Indian Quick Pickled Carrot and Green Chilli
recipes.summary: Tangy carrot batons with mustard seed and turmeric, for curries and rice.
steps: Heat the oil and fry the mustard seeds for 30 seconds, until they pop.
Add the turmeric, chilli flakes, vinegar, sugar and salt and bring to a simmer for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the hot brine over the carrots and chillies in a jar and press to submerge.
Cool, then chill for at least 2 hours.
notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
Add a few lime wedges for extra tang.

recipes.title: Middle Eastern Quick Pickled Radish and Beetroot
recipes.summary: Bright pink wedges of radish and beetroot for falafel, shawarma and mezze.

items: 1 raw beetroot, cut in thin wedges

steps: Pack the radish and beetroot into a clean jar with the garlic and bay leaf.
Simmer the water, vinegar and salt for 3 minutes, until the salt dissolves.
Pour the hot brine over the vegetables, leaving them fully covered.
Cool, then chill for 2 days, until pink all through.
notes: Keeps for 3 weeks in the fridge.
Wear gloves to avoid pink hands.

recipes.title: Korean Quick Pickled Radish Slices
recipes.summary: Crisp and sweet pickled radish slices that cut through fried chicken and rich barbecue meat.
steps: Pack the radish rounds into a jar.
Heat the vinegar, sugar, water, salt and peppercorns for 2 minutes, until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the hot brine over the radish and cool.
Chill for 2 hours before serving.
notes: Add a few drops of yellow food colouring if you like it bright.
Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.

recipes.title: Quick Pickled Jalapenos
recipes.summary: Crunchy, fiery rings to pile on nachos, burgers and tacos.
steps: Pack the jalapeno rings into a jar with the garlic and cumin seeds.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar and salt for 2 minutes, until dissolved.
Pour the hot brine over the chillies until covered.
Cool, then chill for 1 day.
notes: Wear gloves when slicing the chillies.
Keeps for 1 month in the fridge.

recipes.title: Quick Pickled Celery and Orange
recipes.summary: Crisp celery slices and orange peel in a sweet vinegar brine, lovely with fish, ham and salads.
steps: Pack the celery into a jar with the orange zest.
Warm the orange juice, vinegar, water, sugar, salt and fennel seeds for 2 minutes, until dissolved.
Pour the warm brine over the celery until covered.
Cool, then chill for 1 hour.
notes: Eat within 5 days.
Spoon onto grilled fish or ham sandwiches.

recipes.title: Swedish Dill Pickled Cucumber Slices
recipes.summary: Paper-thin cucumber slices in a sweet vinegar brine with dill, a Swedish table staple for meatballs and salmon.
steps: Whisk the vinegar, sugar, water, salt and pepper until the sugar dissolves.
Layer the cucumber and dill in a bowl.
Pour over the brine and press down until submerged.
Chill for 1 hour and drain before serving.
notes: Slice thinly with a mandoline.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Mexican Eggs Under Red and Green Salsa with Beans
recipes.summary: Two fried eggs "divorced" by a line of refried beans, one under red salsa and one under green salsa.

items: 200g tinned black beans, mashed and warmed

steps: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each, until soft and flecked, and keep warm.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the edges crisp.
Place 2 tortillas on each plate and top each with an egg.
Spoon red salsa over one egg and green over the other, with a line of warm beans between.
Scatter with cheese, onion and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the yolks thickened, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Use your favourite jarred salsas to save time.

recipes.title: Mexican Sopa de Frijol Black Bean Soup
recipes.summary: A smoky, thick black bean soup with cumin and chipotle, topped with sour cream, coriander and lime.
steps: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beans, chipotle, stock, tomatoes and salt and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick.
Blend half the soup until smooth and stir back in.
Serve with sour cream, coriander and lime.
notes: Blend more for a smoother soup.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

recipes.title: Mexican Albondigas Soup Meatball Vegetable Soup
recipes.summary: Tender beef and rice meatballs poached in a tomato broth with carrot, zucchini and potato.
steps: Mix the beef, rice, egg, oregano, cumin, 1 tsp salt, half the garlic and the mint, and roll into 24 small balls.
Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and remaining garlic for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes, stock, carrots, potato and remaining salt and bring to a simmer, until bubbling gently.
Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 20 minutes, until the meatballs are cooked through and the potato is tender.
Add the zucchini for the last 5 minutes and serve with coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink inside, wash hands after handling raw mince, and chill leftovers within 2 hours.
Do not stir for the first 5 minutes, so the meatballs set.

recipes.title: Australian Corn Fritters with Avocado and Tomato
recipes.summary: Golden corn fritters with smashed avocado, tomato and a squeeze of lime, a cafe brunch classic.
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, eggs, milk, salt and paprika into a thick batter.
Fold in the corn, spring onions and coriander.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry spoonfuls of the batter for 3 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Serve the fritters with avocado and tomato slices.
notes: Food safety: make sure the fritters are cooked through, as raw egg batter is unsafe; keep egg dishes chilled and eat within 2 days.
Keep warm in a 100C oven while frying the rest.

recipes.title: Scottish Creamy Leek, Potato and Fish Soup
recipes.summary: A creamy soup of poached cod, potato and leek with a pinch of smoked paprika.
steps: Poach the cod in the milk with the bay leaf for 8 minutes, until it flakes easily, then lift out, flake and discard the skin and bones.
Melt the butter in a pot and cook the leek and onion for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the potatoes and fish stock and simmer for 12 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Pour in the poaching milk and mash roughly with a fork to thicken.
Return the fish with the cream and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and heat for 3 minutes without boiling, then add pepper and parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook fish until it flakes easily and is opaque all through, chill leftovers within 2 hours, and eat within 2 days.
Add a pinch of salt at the end if needed.

recipes.title: American Corn Chowder Potato and Sweet Corn
recipes.summary: A thick, creamy chowder of sweet corn, potato and capsicum with a hint of smoked paprika.
steps: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion, celery and capsicum for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the potatoes, half the corn, the stock, paprika and salt and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Blend half the soup until smooth and return it to the pot.
Add the milk, cream and remaining corn and heat for 5 minutes, until hot.
Season with pepper and serve with chives.
notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge; reheat gently.
Use evaporated milk for a lighter chowder.
